tasks.title: Set up Phoenix project with Elixir
tasks.description: Initialize a new Phoenix project with Elixir 1.7+, including dependencies for real-time channels, database, and authentication.
tasks.details: Run `mix phx.new globalbridge_backend --no-ecto` to create the project. Add dependencies: `{:phoenix_live_view, "~> 0.18"}, {:ecto_sql, "~> 3.9"}, {:sqlite_ecto2, "~> 2.3"}, {:jason, "~> 1.3"}`. Configure SQLite as the database in `config/dev.exs`. Set up basic folder structure as per PRD. Note: Database architecture uses sharding strategy where each thread/conversation gets its own SQLite database file (e.g., `threads/{thread_id}.db`) for granular backup, sharing, and E2EE. Shared databases include `users.db`, `bridges.db`, and `sync_state.db`.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify project compiles and starts with `mix phx.server`. Check that SQLite database is created and migrations run.

tasks.title: Implement database schema for users, threads, and messages
tasks.description: Create Ecto schemas and migrations for core tables: users, threads, messages, bridges, and CDC log, accounting for per-thread database sharding.
tasks.details: Define schemas in `lib/messaging/` with fields as per PRD. Create migrations: `mix ecto.gen.migration create_users`, etc. Use SQLite with foreign keys. For CDC log, add triggers to capture changes. Implement sharding strategy: each thread/conversation gets its own SQLite database file (e.g., `priv/db/threads/{thread_id}.db`) for messages and thread-specific data. Shared databases: `users.db` (global users), `bridges.db` (bridge configurations), `sync_state.db` (CDC sync tracking). Messages and thread data are stored in per-thread databases to enable granular backup, sharing, and E2EE with per-thread encryption keys.
tasks.testStrategy: Run migrations and verify tables exist in SQLite. Insert test data and check relationships. Test database sharding by creating multiple thread databases and verifying isolation.

tasks.title: Set up iOS project with Swift 6 and SwiftUI
tasks.description: Initialize Xcode project for iOS app with Swift 6 strict concurrency, SwiftUI, and required dependencies.
tasks.details: COMPLETE STEP-BY-STEP XCODE SETUP (for users new to Xcode): 1) Install Xcode from Mac App Store (search 'Xcode', ~12GB download). 2) Launch Xcode and create new project: File → New → Project → iOS App → SwiftUI interface → Swift language → Product Name: 'GlobalBridge' → Team: None → Organization Identifier: 'com.yourname.globalbridge' → Save in clients/ios folder. 3) Configure project: Select project → GlobalBridge target → General tab: iOS 15.0+ deployment target → Build Settings: Swift Language Version = 6, Strict Concurrency Checking = Complete. 4) Create folder structure: Right-click GlobalBridge folder → New Group for 'Core' and 'Features' → Add subgroups: Core/Models, Core/Networking, Core/Storage, Core/Crypto, Features/Threads, Features/Chat, Features/Bridges. 5) Add packages: File → Add Packages → Add 'https://github.com/davidstump/SwiftPhoenixClient' and 'https://github.com/stephencelis/SQLite.swift'. 6) Clean up: Replace GlobalBridgeApp.swift content, create ContentView.swift with basic Text view. 7) Build and run on iOS simulator.
tasks.testStrategy: Build and run on simulator. Verify SwiftUI views render correctly. Check that packages resolve without errors. Confirm folder structure matches PRD. Verify Swift 6 strict concurrency is enabled. Test that project builds successfully.
